parsed_output.analysis: The specification describes a top-level flow DoorsClosing → InMotion with InMotion containing the three motion substates Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching and two exits from InMotion to Stopping and EmergencyStopping, plus specific entry/exit actions and signals for the substates and for EmergencyStopping. The PlantUML model implements most of the structure but diverges on signals/actions, initialisation and the behaviour of Approaching/EmergencyStopping.

issues.issue: Initial state of the top-level machine is not made explicit
issues.reason: Specification 1 states the system starts in DoorsClosing. The model defines DoorsClosing and a DoorsClosing --> InMotion transition but contains no [*] --> DoorsClosing initial pseudostate, so the start state is not explicit in the diagram.

issues.issue: Stopping transition label mismatches the specified signal/action name
issues.reason: Specification 2 requires the transition to be triggered by “Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived”. The model uses “Arrived/Stop, SendArrived” – SendArrived vs Send Arrived – a naming/ spacing mismatch that does not match the specification.

issues.issue: EmergencyStopping does not model sending the Obstacle Detected signal
issues.reason: Specification 3 requires EmergencyStopping to include the action Emergency Stop and to send the “Obstacle Detected” signal. The model shows Entry: Emergency Stop but represents Obstacle Detected only as a state note “EmergencyStopping: Obstacle Detected”. No send action/effect is shown and the transition InMotion --> EmergencyStopping is labelled Obstacle Detected as a trigger, conflating trigger with the required outgoing signal.
issues.where: State EmergencyStopping and transition InMotion --> EmergencyStopping

issues.issue: Approaching substate does not send the required Send signal
issues.reason: Specification 9 requires that in the Approaching substate the system sends the “Send” signal and continues to approach the destination. The model defines Approaching with only the notes “Nearing Destination” and “Ready to Stop/Decelerate” and contains no send action/effect for a Send signal.

issues.issue: Approaching substate behaviour for remaining until ready to stop/decelerate is not modelled as behaviour
issues.reason: Specification 10 requires the system to remain in Approaching while nearing the destination until it is ready to stop or decelerate. The model only annotates Approaching with the static notes “Nearing Destination” and “Ready to Stop/Decelerate” and provides no self-loop, guard or outgoing transition that captures remaining in the substate and exiting when ready to stop/decelerate.

issues.issue: Accelerate entry action is placed on the internal initial transition rather than as a state entry
issues.reason: Specification 8 states the Accelerating substate is entered when motion begins, marked by the “Entry/Accelerate” action. The model puts Entry/Accelerate on the [*] --> Accelerating transition label instead of modelling it as an entry action of the Accelerating state, which is a semantic deviation from the specified entry marking.

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1. The system starts in the DoorsClosing state and transitions to InMotion when the doors are closed, triggered by the "Closed/SendDeparted" signal. 
2. In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected. 
3. When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal. 
4. Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, which represent different phases of the train's motion. 
5. The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal. 
6. If the system is in the Accelerating substate and approaches its destination, it transitions to the Approaching substate upon receiving the "Approached/Decelerate" signal. 
7. The system in the Cruising substate transitions to the Approaching substate when it approaches the destination, triggered by the "Approached/Decelerate" signal. 
8. The system enters the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action. 
9. In the Approaching substate, the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination. 
10. The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate.

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
state DoorsClosing

DoorsClosing --> InMotion: Closed/SendDeparted

state InMotion {
[*] --> Accelerating : Entry/Accelerate
Accelerating --> Cruising : Reached Cruising/Cruise
Accelerating --> Approaching : Approached/Decelerate
Cruising --> Approaching : Approached/Decelerate

state Accelerating
state Cruising
state Approaching {
Approaching: Nearing Destination
Approaching: Ready to Stop/Decelerate
}
}

InMotion --> Stopping: Arrived/Stop, SendArrived
InMotion --> EmergencyStopping: Obstacle Detected

state Stopping
state EmergencyStopping {
Entry: Emergency Stop
EmergencyStopping: Obstacle Detected
}
@enduml
